Welcome to Bali Eling Spirit

Your Divine Home to Transform

Start Your Meditation

Authentic Balinese Spiritual Wellness

A Legacy of Sacred Healing Across Generations

Bali Eling Spirit is a spiritual wellness sanctuary rooted in authentic Balinese wisdom, preserving a sacred legacy of healing passed down across generations through yoga & meditation. Internationally accredited, Bali Eling Spirit is a trusted institution for professional yoga teacher training, proudly offering its signature method, Bali Hatha Yoga – a unique yoga sequence and methodology created by the founder of Bali Eling Spirit.

“Bali Hatha Yoga was born from contemplation, practice, and revelation—a path of balance where the body becomes a temple, the breath becomes prayer, and movement becomes a medium of healing that unites the inner and outer universe.”

Sri Bhagawan Sriprada Bhaskara (Founder Bali Eling Spirit)

items.post_content:
This is a sample page.

Overview

Our refund and returns policy lasts 30 days. If 30 days have passed since your purchase, we can’t offer you a full refund or exchange.

To be eligible for a return, your item must be unused and in the same condition that you received it. It must also be in the original packaging.

Several types of goods are exempt from being returned. Perishable goods such as food, flowers, newspapers or magazines cannot be returned. We also do not accept products that are intimate or sanitary goods, hazardous materials, or flammable liquids or gases.

Additional non-returnable items:

  • Gift cards
  • Downloadable software products
  • Some health and personal care items

To complete your return, we require a receipt or proof of purchase.

Please do not send your purchase back to the manufacturer.

There are certain situations where only partial refunds are granted:

  • Book with obvious signs of use
  • CD, DVD, VHS tape, software, video game, cassette tape, or vinyl record that has been opened.
  • Any item not in its original condition, is damaged or missing parts for reasons not due to our error.
  • Any item that is returned more than 30 days after delivery

Refunds

Once your return is received and inspected, we will send you an email to notify you that we have received your returned item. We will also notify you of the approval or rejection of your refund.

If you are approved, then your refund will be processed, and a credit will automatically be applied to your credit card or original method of payment, within a certain amount of days.

Late or missing refunds

If you haven’t received a refund yet, first check your bank account again.

Then contact your credit card company, it may take some time before your refund is officially posted.

Next contact your bank. There is often some processing time before a refund is posted.

If you’ve done all of this and you still have not received your refund yet, please contact us at {email address}.

Sale items

Only regular priced items may be refunded. Sale items cannot be refunded.

Exchanges

We only replace items if they are defective or damaged. If you need to exchange it for the same item, send us an email at {email address} and send your item to: {physical address}.

Gifts

If the item was marked as a gift when purchased and shipped directly to you, you’ll receive a gift credit for the value of your return. Once the returned item is received, a gift certificate will be mailed to you.

If the item wasn’t marked as a gift when purchased, or the gift giver had the order shipped to themselves to give to you later, we will send a refund to the gift giver and they will find out about your return.

Shipping returns

To return your product, you should mail your product to: {physical address}.

You will be responsible for paying for your own shipping costs for returning your item. Shipping costs are non-refundable. If you receive a refund, the cost of return shipping will be deducted from your refund.

Depending on where you live, the time it may take for your exchanged product to reach you may vary.

If you are returning more expensive items, you may consider using a trackable shipping service or purchasing shipping insurance. We don’t guarantee that we will receive your returned item.

Need help?

Contact us at {email} for questions related to refunds and returns.

items.title: Eling Sound Awakening
items.post_content:
An Evening Practice of Sound, Stillness, and Awareness

Eling Sound Awakening is a guided evening sound-healing experience at Bali Eling Spirit for people who want to slow down, release the pressure of the day, and return to a quieter inner rhythm. The word eling points to awareness: the simple but powerful act of remembering yourself beneath noise, routine, and constant mental activity. This session creates a gentle space for that remembering through breath, meditation, sacred sound, and unhurried rest.

The experience is designed as a companion to the sanctuary’s morning practices, but it also stands fully on its own. You do not need previous experience with meditation, yoga, sound healing, or Balinese spiritual practice. The team guides each stage clearly, allowing beginners and experienced practitioners to participate at a pace that feels natural.

What to Expect During the Session

Your visit begins with a calm arrival and a short orientation. You will be invited to settle into the space, notice your breathing, and set a personal intention for the evening. Nothing needs to be forced or performed. The opening is simply a transition from the activity outside the sanctuary to a more receptive state inside it.

The central practice uses resonant instruments, including singing bowls and other traditional sound elements, together with guided silence and Balinese mantra. Sound is offered as an object of attention and a support for deep rest. Some participants notice physical relaxation, others experience clearer awareness, and others simply enjoy the rare opportunity to be still without having to achieve anything. Every response is valid.

The session closes gradually rather than abruptly. Time is provided to return attention to the body, breathe normally, and integrate the experience before leaving. The facilitator may offer a short reflection or a simple practice that can be continued at home. The intention is not to promise an instant cure, but to create a meaningful pause that supports balance, presence, and self-awareness.

Who This Experience May Suit

  • Travelers who want a restorative evening after a full day in Bali.
  • Busy professionals carrying mental fatigue or constant screen exposure.
  • Beginners who are curious about meditation or sound-based practice.
  • Returning guests who want to deepen the calm created by a morning program.
  • Anyone seeking a respectful, non-judgmental sanctuary experience.

Eling Sound Awakening is not a replacement for medical or psychological care. Guests with specific health concerns, pregnancy, sound sensitivity, or mobility needs should mention them during booking so the team can advise on a comfortable arrangement.

Participation can be quiet and personal. You are not expected to share private experiences with the group, adopt a particular belief, or react to the sounds in a certain way. The most helpful approach is to listen, notice, and let the facilitator’s instructions support a safe transition between alertness, rest, and reflection.

Preparing for Your Visit

Wear modest, comfortable clothing that allows you to sit or lie down with ease. Arrive a little early so the session can begin without rushing. It is helpful to reduce phone use before entering, eat lightly, and bring an open but unforced attitude. Mats and session equipment are provided by the sanctuary; ask the team during booking if you need extra physical support.

Availability is generally offered on sanctuary operating days and may change around ceremonies, teacher schedules, or private programs. Confirm the current time, price, tax, and meeting point directly with the Bali Eling Spirit team before traveling. Advance reservation is recommended because the atmosphere works best in a carefully held group.

Continue the Journey

Guests who want a fuller day may combine the evening session with Sacred Morning Awakening or explore the longer experiences listed on the Sanctuary page. To ask about availability, private arrangements, or the best program for your needs, contact the team through the website’s WhatsApp enquiry option.

items.title: Session with the Founder with Aji Bhagawan
items.post_content:
A Private Conversation for Clarity and Spiritual Direction

Session with the Founder is a private, request-based meeting for guests who want focused spiritual guidance from Aji Bhagawan within the Bali Eling Spirit tradition. It is intended for moments when a general class or group retreat does not fully address the questions you are carrying. The session offers time to speak honestly, listen carefully, and consider the next step in your personal practice.

People arrive with many kinds of questions: a loss of direction, repeated emotional patterns, difficulty maintaining a spiritual routine, uncertainty about which retreat to choose, or a desire to understand how yoga, meditation, Dharma, and daily responsibility can support one another. The meeting is not built around a fixed script. Its value comes from attention to your actual situation and from guidance grounded in the practices taught at Bali Eling Spirit.

What the Session Can Explore

  • Your present spiritual concerns and the patterns you want to understand.
  • A practical meditation, breath, or awareness routine suited to daily life.
  • How to prepare for a retreat, teacher training, or deeper period of practice.
  • Ways to integrate insights from previous healing or retreat experiences.
  • Questions about purpose, discipline, relationships, service, and personal responsibility.

The session may include conversation, guided reflection, a simple contemplative practice, or recommendations for continued study. It does not guarantee a particular outcome, predict the future, or replace professional medical, psychiatric, psychological, legal, or financial advice. The purpose is spiritual education and personal reflection in a respectful setting.

Because the meeting is individual, the discussion should remain grounded in what can be understood and practised responsibly. Aji Bhagawan may redirect broad or abstract questions toward concrete choices, awareness, and conduct. This keeps the session useful beyond the meeting and helps translate spiritual insight into daily relationships, work, service, and self-discipline.

How to Prepare

Before arriving, write down the two or three questions that matter most. Clear questions help the meeting remain focused. You may also bring a journal to record key points after the session. There is no need to prepare a polished story or disclose anything you do not wish to discuss. Honest simplicity is more useful than trying to present yourself in a particular way.

Please wear modest, comfortable clothing appropriate for a sacred learning environment. Arrive with enough time to settle. Phones should be silenced during the meeting so the conversation can remain private and uninterrupted. Translation support or a companion may be requested in advance, subject to the team’s approval and the confidential nature of the session.

Availability and Booking

Founder sessions are offered by request and depend on Aji Bhagawan’s teaching, retreat, ceremony, and travel schedule. A request is not confirmed until the Bali Eling Spirit team has replied with an agreed date, time, format, and contribution. The team may recommend a session with an authorized Yogi when that is more suitable or available sooner.

When enquiring, share your preferred dates, language, whether you are already enrolled in another program, and a short description of what you hope to explore. Avoid sending highly sensitive personal records through public messaging channels. The team can advise on the most appropriate way to provide essential background.

After the Meeting

The most useful part of guidance often begins after the conversation. Leave space to reflect, review your notes, and practise any recommendation consistently before judging its value. A follow-up session or a suitable sanctuary program may be suggested, but there is no obligation to continue. The aim is to support a clearer, more responsible relationship with your own path.

To request a session, use the WhatsApp enquiry option on the About Bali Eling Spirit page and state that you are asking about a private session with Aji Bhagawan.

items.title: Eling Retreat
items.post_content:
A Short Retreat for Release, Balance, and Return

Eling Retreat is a focused sanctuary experience created for people who need meaningful time to step away from routine without committing to a multi-day residential program. Rooted in the Bali Eling Spirit approach, it brings together mindful movement, meditation, breath, purification, sound, and reflection in one coherent journey. The intention is simple: to help you release accumulated tension, restore awareness, and return to daily life with greater clarity.

The retreat has traditionally been connected with Tilem, the Balinese dark-moon period associated with introspection and cleansing. Current dates, duration, and session structure may vary according to the ceremonial calendar and the availability of the teaching team. Guests should always confirm the next intake before making travel plans.

How the Journey Unfolds

The day begins with grounding and intention setting. You are invited to put aside the pace of the outside world and notice what is present in the body, breath, and mind. Gentle Bali Hatha Yoga and pranayama support physical openness without requiring advanced flexibility or previous experience.

Guided meditation then creates space to observe thoughts and emotions without immediately reacting to them. Depending on the confirmed program, the retreat may also include a Balinese purification element, reflective teaching, sacred sound, or a shared vegetarian meal. Each part is arranged to support the next, so the experience feels like a complete arc rather than a collection of unrelated activities.

The closing period is intentionally unhurried. Participants are encouraged to reflect on what they noticed, identify one practical change to carry home, and avoid rushing straight back into constant phone use or a crowded schedule. The aim is not to escape life, but to re-enter it with more awareness.

Group size and the exact flow can differ from one date to another. Some sessions may place more emphasis on movement and meditation, while ceremonial dates may shape the purification or reflective elements. This flexibility protects the integrity of the experience. The booking confirmation, rather than an archived description, should be treated as the final guide for your chosen date.

Who May Benefit

  • People experiencing mental fatigue, emotional heaviness, or loss of focus.
  • Travelers seeking an authentic short-format spiritual retreat in Bali.
  • Beginners who want guided exposure to yoga, meditation, and purification.
  • Returning guests who feel called to practise around the Tilem period.
  • Those considering a longer retreat and wanting an appropriate first step.

Eling Retreat is educational and spiritual in nature. It does not promise medical treatment, trauma resolution, or guaranteed healing. Inform the team in advance about injuries, pregnancy, significant health conditions, or accessibility needs so they can advise whether the current format is suitable.

What to Bring and How to Prepare

Choose comfortable, modest clothing for movement and sacred spaces. Bring a refillable water bottle and a journal if you enjoy writing. The sanctuary provides the main practice equipment. Eat lightly before arrival unless the booking team gives different instructions, and arrive early enough to settle without stress.

Because the retreat may follow the Balinese lunar and ceremonial calendar, advance booking is essential. Ask the team to confirm the date, starting time, inclusions, price, tax, transport arrangements, and whether the session is shared or private. Do not rely on an old event listing when arranging transportation.

Choosing the Right Depth

Guests who prefer a daily half-day experience can explore the Healing Retreat. Those needing a longer residential pause can consider the Eling Sanctuary Retreat, while deeper four-day work is described on the Eling Tapa Brata page. The sanctuary team can help you choose honestly based on your available time and readiness.

Use the WhatsApp enquiry option on the Sanctuary page to ask for the next Eling Retreat date and current booking information.

items.title: Personal Eling Session with the Yogi
items.post_content:
One-to-One Guidance for Your Present Needs

Personal Eling Session with the Yogi is a private, guided experience for guests who want individual attention rather than a group program. The session is shaped around where you are now: your energy, experience level, questions, physical comfort, and the amount of time available. It offers a practical way to explore the Bali Eling Spirit approach through awareness, breath, meditation, movement, and reflective guidance.

Eling means remembering or returning to awareness. In a personal session, that principle becomes direct and specific. Instead of following a fixed class plan, you work with an authorized Yogi who can adjust the pace, explain the purpose of each practice, and help you notice how the body, breath, thoughts, and emotions influence one another.

Possible Areas of Focus

  • Foundational meditation for a busy or overactive mind.
  • Gentle Bali Hatha Yoga adapted to your current ability.
  • Pranayama and breath awareness for grounding and concentration.
  • Reflection on personal patterns, discipline, and daily spiritual practice.
  • Preparation for a retreat, teacher training, purification, or sound session.
  • Integration after a previous Bali Eling Spirit program.

The final structure is confirmed after a short conversation with the booking team or Yogi. A session may emphasize practice, discussion, or a balanced combination of both. No special belief system is required. Guests from different religious, spiritual, or non-religious backgrounds are welcome when they approach the sanctuary and its Balinese traditions with respect.

The first minutes are usually used to clarify your intention and agree on a realistic focus. This prevents the session from becoming too broad and gives the Yogi enough context to choose an appropriate sequence. Practices can be slowed down, simplified, or explained in greater detail, making the private format useful for both complete beginners and experienced guests who want to refine their foundations. You remain free to pause, ask questions, or decline any practice that does not feel appropriate.

What the Session Is—and Is Not

This is a spiritual and educational session, not medical treatment or psychotherapy. It does not diagnose illness, replace prescribed care, guarantee healing, or offer certainty about future events. Guests dealing with acute physical or mental-health concerns should continue working with qualified professionals and tell the team about any relevant limitations before booking.

Privacy is treated respectfully, but participants should avoid sending unnecessary sensitive documents through ordinary messaging. Share only the information required for safe and appropriate guidance. If a request falls outside the Yogi’s role, the team may suggest another program or advise you to seek a different kind of professional support.

Preparing for a Personal Session

Wear comfortable, modest clothing that allows gentle movement and seated practice. Bring a journal, water, and one or two clear intentions. Arrive early, silence your phone, and allow a little quiet time after the session rather than scheduling an immediate rush to the next activity.

During booking, state your preferred language, available dates, previous yoga or meditation experience, injuries or access needs, and whether you prefer a practice-focused or guidance-focused meeting. The team will confirm the duration, facilitator, contribution, location, and any preparation specific to your session.

Continuing After the Session

A personal session can be complete in itself or serve as a beginning. Your Yogi may recommend a simple daily practice, a group meditation course, a sanctuary retreat, or teacher training when appropriate. Give the recommendation time and consistency; inner work becomes meaningful through regular application rather than intensity alone.

To request a private appointment, contact the Bali Eling Spirit team through the website’s WhatsApp option and mention “Personal Eling Session with the Yogi.” You can also review the Sanctuary programs and the Eling Meditation Course before deciding.

items.title: Contact Bali Eling Spirit
items.post_content:
Begin Your Enquiry

Contact Bali Eling Spirit to ask about retreat availability, yoga teacher training, meditation courses, private guidance, workshops, transport arrangements, or the best program for your current needs. The team can help you compare options without pressure and confirm the practical details that may change with the teaching and ceremonial calendar.

Location

Bali Eling Spirit is located in Pejeng Kangin, Tampaksiring, Gianyar, Bali 80552, Indonesia, in a quiet area within reach of Ubud. Ask the team for the current map pin, meeting point, and transfer instructions before departure. Some programs include or arrange transport from a specified pickup point, while others require guests to travel directly to the sanctuary.

WhatsApp and Telephone

For booking questions, use the website’s WhatsApp button or call +62 878 2598 9117. Include your name, preferred program, proposed dates, number of participants, language, and any mobility or dietary needs. A booking is only confirmed after the team replies with availability and the required next steps.

Email

For detailed enquiries, partnerships, media requests, or documents, email balielingspirit@elinggroup.com. Avoid sending passport copies, health records, or other sensitive information until the team explains the secure and necessary process.

Before You Travel

  • Confirm the exact date, starting time, duration, inclusions, and current price.
  • Ask what clothing, identification, or personal items are required.
  • Share relevant injuries, pregnancy, allergies, or access needs in advance.
  • Confirm cancellation, rescheduling, tax, service, and payment terms.
  • Request the current location pin and pickup instructions.

The sanctuary welcomes guests from many backgrounds. Please approach the space with modest clothing, respectful conduct, and willingness to follow guidance around ceremonies, photography, silence, and shared practice.

For a quick overview before contacting the team, visit the Sanctuary, Yoga Teacher Training, and Wisdom pages.

items.title: Private Sacred Sessions
items.post_content:
Private Guidance, Shaped Around the Person

Private Sacred Sessions at Bali Eling Spirit are request-based, one-to-one experiences for guests who need more individual attention than a group class or retreat can provide. They are designed for moments when you want to slow down, clarify what you are carrying, and receive guidance that responds to your present situation rather than following a fixed public program.

The sessions are rooted in the Bali Eling Spirit approach to awareness, yoga, meditation, breath, Dharma, and responsible daily practice. They take place within the sanctuary's respectful Balinese spiritual setting in Pejeng Kangin, Tampaksiring, Gianyar. No particular religious identity or previous experience is required, but guests are expected to approach the teachers, practices, and sacred environment with sincerity and respect.

Choose the Kind of Support You Need

Session with the Founder with Aji Bhagawan

This private conversation is intended for guests seeking focused spiritual direction from Aji Bhagawan. It may be suitable when you are facing repeated emotional or behavioural patterns, uncertainty about your direction, difficulty maintaining a meaningful spiritual routine, questions about purpose and responsibility, or a need to understand which Bali Eling Spirit program is appropriate for your next step.

The meeting may include conversation, guided reflection, a simple contemplative practice, or recommendations for continued study. Because availability follows Aji Bhagawan's teaching, ceremony, retreat, and travel schedule, every request must be confirmed directly by the Bali Eling Spirit team. Read the full Session with the Founder details.

Personal Eling Session with the Yogi

This private guided session is more practice-oriented and can be adjusted to your experience, physical comfort, questions, and available time. Possible areas of focus include foundational meditation, gentle Bali Hatha Yoga, pranayama and breath awareness, grounding, reflective guidance, preparation for a retreat or teacher training, and integration after a previous Bali Eling Spirit experience.

An authorized Yogi can slow the pace, explain the purpose of each practice, and help you observe how body, breath, thoughts, and emotions influence one another. The final structure may emphasize practice, conversation, or a balanced combination of both. Read the full Personal Eling Session details.

What These Sessions Are—and Are Not

Private Sacred Sessions are spiritual and educational experiences. They do not diagnose illness, replace medical or psychological care, guarantee healing, predict future events, or provide legal, financial, or clinical advice. Guests with acute physical or mental-health concerns should continue working with qualified professionals and tell the booking team about any relevant limitations before participating.

You remain free to ask questions, pause, or decline a practice that does not feel appropriate. Privacy is treated respectfully, but guests should avoid sending unnecessary health records, identity documents, or other sensitive files through ordinary messaging channels. Share only what is needed for safe and suitable guidance.

How to Prepare

Before contacting the team, identify one or two clear intentions. Include your preferred dates, language, previous yoga or meditation experience, any injuries or access needs, and whether you are looking mainly for spiritual direction, practical instruction, or support choosing a longer program. Wear modest, comfortable clothing and allow quiet time after the session instead of scheduling an immediate rush to another activity.

Duration, facilitator, contribution, location, translation support, and preparation requirements are confirmed individually. A request is not a confirmed booking until the Bali Eling Spirit team replies with the agreed details.

Request a Private Sacred Session

Use the Bali Eling Spirit contact page or the website's WhatsApp option. State whether you are asking for a Session with the Founder or a Personal Eling Session with the Yogi, then briefly describe what you hope to explore. When another sanctuary program would serve you better, the team may recommend that path instead.

items.title: Sound Chakra Healing
items.post_content:
A Guided Practice of Sound, Stillness, and Awareness

Sound Chakra Healing at Bali Eling Spirit is presented as a gentle, guided experience for people who want to slow down, become more aware of their inner state, and rest in a carefully held sanctuary setting. The approach reflects the same principles described in the current Eling Sound Awakening program: breath, meditation, resonant sound, silence, and gradual integration are used to support attention and relaxation without asking participants to perform or force a particular response. Singing bowls and other sound elements may be used as objects of concentration while the facilitator guides the group toward a quieter rhythm. Some guests notice that the body softens, the breath becomes steadier, or mental activity feels less dominant; others simply value having protected time to listen and be still. The practice is spiritual and contemplative rather than medical, and it should not be described as a cure or a replacement for qualified physical or mental-health care.

What to Expect During the Experience

A typical visit begins with an unhurried arrival, a short orientation, and an invitation to set a personal intention. Participants are then guided through simple breathing or meditation so attention can move away from the pace of the day and toward present-moment awareness. The central sound practice may combine Tibetan singing bowls, mantra, periods of silence, and other resonant instruments used within Bali Eling Spirit's broader healing and retreat work. There is no requirement to have previous experience with yoga, meditation, chakra practice, or sound healing, and there is no expectation that participants disclose private experiences to a group. The closing is intentionally gradual, allowing time to notice the body, return to normal breathing, and reflect before leaving. Because facilitator availability, ceremonial dates, group size, and session format can change, the exact structure should always be confirmed with the Bali Eling Spirit team when making a reservation.

Sound, Chakras, and Responsible Expectations

In this context, the word chakra provides a spiritual map for paying attention to different qualities of experience; it should not be used to diagnose illness or to promise that a single session will remove a physical or psychological condition. Bali Eling Spirit's wider teaching repeatedly connects body, mind and feeling, and deeper awareness, so the sound practice is best approached as one part of a broader discipline of listening, breathing, reflection, and conscious living. Participants are free to receive the experience according to their own background, and they are not required to adopt unfamiliar beliefs or describe sensations in a prescribed way. Respect for Balinese-Hindu elements, the facilitator's boundaries, and the privacy of other guests is essential. Photography, recording, or promotional use of a session should only occur with explicit permission, especially when a group is using the space for quiet personal work.

Preparing and Choosing the Right Program

Guests are encouraged to wear modest, comfortable clothing that makes it easy to sit or lie down, arrive early enough to settle without rushing, and avoid a heavy meal immediately before the session. Anyone who is pregnant, sensitive to sound, managing a medical condition, or needing mobility support should share that information during booking so the team can advise whether the current arrangement is suitable. Prices, taxes, start times, language support, private-session options, and available dates should be verified directly rather than assumed from an older listing. Visitors who are looking specifically for the sanctuary's established evening format can also review the Eling Sound Awakening page, while those seeking a longer combination of yoga, breathwork, meditation, cleansing practice, and sound may explore the wider sanctuary and retreat offerings. Contacting the team before traveling is the best way to select the experience that matches your needs and the current program calendar.

items.title: 7 Chakra Crystal Healing
items.post_content:
A Balinese-Inspired Chakra Purification Practice

The 7 Chakra Crystal Healing page introduces a self-cleansing and awareness practice connected to Bali Eling Spirit's established 7-Chakra Purification work. Within the Pasraman's spiritual framework, the seven chakras are understood as important centers in the body's subtle-energy system, and the practice is intended to help participants reflect on balance across the physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual dimensions of life. Bali Eling Spirit describes its purification approach as combining holy water, mantra, meditation energy, and crystals in a guided ceremonial setting. These elements are not presented as a substitute for medicine or psychotherapy, and no specific health outcome can be guaranteed. The purpose of the experience is to offer a respectful container for contemplation, release, prayer, and renewed awareness while remaining rooted in the living Balinese-Hindu context from which the ritual is shared.

How the Session Is Held

The experience normally begins with an introduction to the seven-chakra concept and a guided period of meditation so participants can arrive mentally and emotionally before the ceremonial work begins. The facilitator then leads the purification process using the materials and prayers appropriate to the Pasraman's tradition, which may include specially prepared water, mantra, meditative attention, and crystals. Participants are asked to follow instructions carefully, maintain a respectful atmosphere, and allow the process to unfold without comparing their response with anyone else's. People may experience the ceremony as quiet, emotional, reflective, or simply unfamiliar, and all of those responses can be approached without pressure. The program is open to guests from different backgrounds, but it remains a culturally specific spiritual practice rather than a generic spa treatment. Current facilitators, language support, group size, dates, and the exact sequence should be confirmed directly with the team because ceremonial calendars and operational arrangements may change.

Cultural Respect and Informed Participation

Because this work draws from Balinese spiritual practice, the ceremony should be entered as a guest of a living tradition rather than treated as a decorative wellness activity. Participants should listen to the explanation offered by the team, ask questions respectfully, and avoid making public claims about the ritual that go beyond what they personally experienced or what Bali Eling Spirit has confirmed. Crystals, holy water, mantra, and chakra language can carry different meanings across cultures; on this page they refer specifically to the Pasraman's own guided practice. Consent and privacy also matter. No participant should be pressured to be photographed, to share an emotional response, or to continue if they feel unwell. A responsible booking conversation gives the team enough information to advise on practical comfort while helping the guest understand that spiritual support and clinical health care have different roles. This clarity helps preserve both safety and the integrity of the ceremony.

What to Bring and How to Book

Before attending, ask the Bali Eling Spirit team what clothing, towel, change of clothes, or traditional attire is required for the date you are considering, as water-based purification can involve practical preparation that differs from an ordinary meditation class. Arrive at the confirmed meeting time, follow any guidance about food or personal items, and disclose relevant mobility needs, pregnancy, sound sensitivity, or medical concerns so the team can give appropriate advice. Advance reservation is recommended because the ritual may be linked to specific ceremonial days or facilitator availability, and walk-in participation should not be assumed. Guests can also read the current 7-Chakra Purification information and the sanctuary's broader retreat pages before choosing a program. The most accurate way to proceed is to contact the team through the website or WhatsApp, request the current schedule and inclusions, and confirm whether this focused ceremony or a longer retreat is the better match.

items.title: Partnership
items.post_content:
Purpose-Led Partnerships with Bali Eling Spirit

Bali Eling Spirit welcomes thoughtful partnership conversations with organizations and professionals whose work is genuinely aligned with yoga education, mindful living, retreat experiences, Balinese culture, personal development, and responsible wellness. The Pasraman is a spiritual sanctuary and learning community in Pejeng Kangin, Tampaksiring, with programs that include yoga teacher training, meditation, healing retreats, sound-based practices, Dharma teaching, and carefully facilitated inner-development experiences. A suitable partnership should respect that identity rather than treating the sanctuary as a generic venue or promotional backdrop. The strongest proposals begin with a clear shared purpose, realistic benefits for participants, respect for the teachers and local community, and an honest understanding of what each party will contribute. The team may need time to consult teachers, operations staff, and community stakeholders before deciding whether an idea is appropriate. Submission of an enquiry does not guarantee acceptance; every idea needs to be reviewed against the Pasraman's values, calendar, capacity, cultural responsibilities, and the wellbeing of guests and students.

Types of Collaboration We Can Discuss

Potential conversations may include educational programs for universities or organizations, wellness and leadership sessions, responsibly designed retreat groups, yoga or meditation learning initiatives, practitioner exchanges, community activities, content or media projects, and collaborations with travel or hospitality partners that can represent the experience accurately. These examples describe areas that may be discussed, not fixed packages or automatic commercial offers. Bali Eling Spirit does not publish unverified claims, guarantee participant outcomes, or accept arrangements that compromise safety, privacy, spiritual integrity, or the quality of facilitation. Proposals involving teachers, ceremonies, filming, brand use, revenue sharing, accommodation, transport, meals, certificates, or exclusive dates require explicit written agreement before they are announced. Where a request falls outside the Pasraman's current expertise or availability, the team may decline it, suggest a smaller first step, or recommend a different format that better protects both the participants and the integrity of the work.

Principles for a Responsible Collaboration

Any joint program should be designed around participant care, truthful communication, cultural respect, and operational clarity. Marketing material must distinguish confirmed facts from aspirations and should never use Bali Eling Spirit's teachers, spiritual language, photographs, testimonials, or logos without approval. The parties should agree in advance on who recruits participants, who handles payments and refunds, who owns participant data, how health or accessibility information is collected, and what happens if weather, ceremony, teacher availability, or another local condition requires a change. Where a collaboration includes education or certification, the exact learning hours, assessment, issuing body, and certificate wording must be documented before promotion. Where it includes a retreat or spiritual practice, the program should preserve appropriate group size, preparation, privacy, and time for integration rather than compressing the experience to meet an unrealistic itinerary.

How to Submit a Partnership Enquiry

A useful first message should identify your organization, the people responsible for the project, the intended audience, the purpose of the collaboration, preferred dates, expected group size, location requirements, language needs, budget framework, and the specific role you are asking Bali Eling Spirit to play. Include links or documents that help the team verify your organization and explain how the proposal supports participants beyond marketing exposure. The team may request a call, additional safeguarding information, a site visit, or a written scope covering responsibilities, payment terms, cancellation, intellectual property, privacy, photography, and use of the Bali Eling Spirit name. Please contact the team through the website's official enquiry channels and allow time for internal review before publishing dates or using any logo. A respectful partnership is built through clarity and mutual accountability, so no collaboration should be represented as confirmed until both sides have approved the final plan in writing.

items.title: Pasraman Bali Eling Spirit
items.post_content:
What a Pasraman Means at Bali Eling Spirit

Pasraman Bali Eling Spirit is a place for guided learning, spiritual practice, and personal transformation in Pejeng Kangin, Tampaksiring, Gianyar, Bali. In the Balinese-Hindu tradition, a pasraman is closer to an ashram or living school than to a hotel, spa, or ordinary activity venue: it is a setting where knowledge is practiced slowly, teachers guide the person in front of them, and discipline is connected with daily life. Bali Eling Spirit traces its formal beginning to February 2018 and describes its purpose through the word eling, meaning a present awareness or remembering of one's deeper nature. The sanctuary was founded by Sri Bhagawan Sriprada Bhaskara and developed together with Jero Ratni, bringing long-term meditation practice, Bali Hatha Yoga, spiritual guidance, chakra-balancing work, and sound-based practice into one community. Visitors are invited to approach the Pasraman with sincerity and curiosity rather than with a demand for instant results.

Practice for Body, Mind, Heart, and Inner Awareness

The programs at Bali Eling Spirit work across what the teaching describes as Sthula Sarira, the physical body; Sukhma Sarira, the subtle dimension of mind and feeling; and Antah Karana Sarira, the deeper inner or causal dimension. Depending on the selected program, a participant may encounter gentle yoga, pranayama, meditation, Dharma reflection, sound healing, spiritual counseling, purification ritual, teacher training, journaling, or periods of silence. The Pasraman's yoga education includes the Bali Hatha Yoga method and internationally structured teacher-training pathways, while its sanctuary programs range from shorter introductory experiences to multi-day retreats. Every program should be understood according to its own current description, schedule, prerequisites, and level of intensity. The team states that guests from different religious and personal backgrounds are welcome; participation does not require adopting a new belief, but it does require respect for the local tradition, the facilitators, other participants, and the boundaries of the program.

A Living School and Community

Learning at a pasraman continues beyond a single class because the emphasis is not only on collecting information but on translating practice into conduct, self-observation, and service. Bali Eling Spirit describes small groups and personal guidance as important parts of its approach, and its teachers continue their own study and spiritual journeys rather than presenting the curriculum as something fixed and finished. This living quality also means that a visitor may encounter different rhythms from a commercial studio: ceremonies, community responsibilities, teacher preparation, and periods of retreat can shape the calendar. The appropriate response is not to expect instant access, but to communicate in advance and follow the guidance given. Guests who come for a short program, students entering teacher training, and participants in deeper retreat work may share the same place while following different commitments, so quiet, punctuality, modest dress, and care for common spaces help protect everyone's practice. This shared discipline is part of the learning environment, not an optional rule added for appearances.

Planning a Respectful Visit

The Pasraman is located in the Tampaksiring area, within the cultural and spiritual landscape of Gianyar and within reach of Ubud, but visitors should confirm the exact meeting point and travel plan before departure. Teacher schedules, ceremonies, retreats, private sessions, and community duties can affect when the team is available, so an advance message is more reliable than arriving without an appointment. Ask which program fits your experience level and intention, what clothing or personal items to bring, whether meals or transport are included, what language will be used, and what the current price, tax, cancellation, and accommodation arrangements are. The About Us, Yoga Teacher Training, and sanctuary program pages provide useful background, while the official contact and WhatsApp channels provide the latest operational details. A visit begins best with honest questions, realistic expectations, and enough time to participate without rushing.
